thread.title: Chips Stocks to Fall on Weaker Than Expected iPhone Demand: Citigroup

author: investopedia.com
title: Chips Stocks to Fall on Weaker Than Expected iPhone Demand: Citigroup
text:
Chips Stocks to Fall on Weaker Than Expected iPhone Demand: Citigroup By Shoshanna Delventhal | November 13, 2018 — 12:44 PM EST
Another team of analysts on the Street has turned more bearish on the chip segment, downgrading shares of semiconductor manufacturer Skyworks Solutions Inc. ( SWKS ) and lowering their stock price target for Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ).
In a note to clients, Citigroup's Atif Malik attributed his downbeat outlook for the chip makers on a weaker-than-expected outlook for Apple Inc.'s ( AAPL ) latest iPhone XR and softer smartphone demand in the key Chinese market, as outlined by CNBC . Weak Chinese Smartphone Demand, Disappointing iPhone XR Sales to Weigh on Chip Makers
"We are downgrading Skyworks Solutions to neutral from buy post the earnings season based on broad smartphone weakness observation in China and disappointing iPhone XR unit sales, which will likely hinder radio frequency semis growth in 2019," wrote Malik. "Additionally, we now think that 5G is a 2020 story versus our prior 2019 view with little upside in 2019 from 5G implementation."
Moving forward, Malik expects 5G to serve as a "meaningful catalyst" for Skyworks in 2020, expanding its total addressable market opportunity by $7 million to $8 million, compared to the current 4G market estimated at $15 million.
Woburn, MA-based Skyworks saw its shares fell 5% on Monday, bringing its YTD loss to 23.5%, compared to a 6.2% decline for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index ( SOXX ) and a 2% return for the S&P 500 over the same period. Malik cut his 12-month price target on Skyworks stock from $116 to $85, representing a 16.7% upside from Monday close.
The Citigroup analyst also lowered his price target on Nvidia from $300 to $270, still reflecting a healthy 42.5% upside from Monday close. He attributed his softer outlook to market multiple compression.
At large, the Street has pressed the brakes on praise of the chip segment, forecasting lower returns after a blowout 2017. In October, analysts Deutsche Bank lowered their 2019 earnings estimates by 5% on average for eight chip stocks, forecasting an accelerated decline in business activity. Bears at Morgan Stanley also reduced their forecasts for the once red-hot segment into the fourth quarter and through 2019, citing an inventory correction, while Goldman has repeatedly cited weakened industry fundamentals and other negative headwinds facing chip makers.
